source.text: דִּבְרֵ֥י נְחֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חֲכַלְיָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י בְחֹֽדֶשׁ־כִּסְלֵיו֙ שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. And it was in [the] month [of] Kislev, [in the] year twenty, and I was in Susa the citadel.

en.L: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. And it came about in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, that I was in Susa the citadel.
en.B: The account of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the citadel of Susa.
en.R: This is the account of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year that King Artaxerxes ruled, I was in the royal fortress in Susa.

es.L: Las palabras de Nehemías hijo de Hacalías. Y sucedió en el mes de Quisleu, en el año veinte, que yo estaba en Susa la ciudadela.
es.B: Relato de Nehemías hijo de Hacalías. En el mes de Quisleu, en el año veinte, yo estaba en la ciudadela de Susa.
es.R: Este es el relato de Nehemías hijo de Hacalías. En el mes de Quisleu, en el año veinte del reinado del rey Artajerjes, yo estaba en la fortaleza real de Susa.

fr.L: Les paroles de Néhémie fils de Hakalia. Et il arriva, au mois de Kislev, la vingtième année, que j’étais à Suse la citadelle.
fr.B: Récit de Néhémie, fils de Hakalia. Au mois de Kislev, la vingtième année, j’étais dans la citadelle de Suse.
fr.R: Voici le récit de Néhémie fils de Hakalia. Au mois de Kislev, la vingtième année du règne du roi Artaxerxès, j’étais dans la forteresse royale de Suse.

sw.L: Maneno ya Nehemia mwana wa Hakalia. Ikawa katika mwezi wa Kislevu, mwaka wa ishirini, nami nilikuwa Shushani ngomeni.
sw.B: Habari za Nehemia mwana wa Hakalia. Katika mwezi wa Kislevu, mwaka wa ishirini, nilikuwa katika ngome ya Shushani.
sw.R: Hii ni habari ya Nehemia mwana wa Hakalia. Katika mwezi wa Kislevu, mwaka wa ishirini wa utawala wa Mfalme Artashasta, nilikuwa katika ngome ya kifalme huko Shushani.

vi.L: Những lời của Nê-hê-mi con trai Ha-ca-lia. Và xảy ra vào tháng Kít-lêu, năm thứ hai mươi, khi tôi đang ở tại thành nội Su-sơ.
vi.B: Lời tường thuật của Nê-hê-mi con trai Ha-ca-lia. Vào tháng Kít-lêu, năm thứ hai mươi, tôi đang ở trong thành nội Su-sơ.
vi.R: Đây là câu chuyện Nê-hê-mi con trai Ha-ca-lia kể lại. Vào tháng Kít-lêu, năm thứ hai mươi đời vua Ạt-ta-xét-xe, tôi đang ở trong hoàng thành Su-sơ.

ko.L: 하가랴의 아들 느헤미야의 말들이다. 기슬르 월, 제20년에, 내가 수산 성에 있었다.
ko.B: 하가랴의 아들 느헤미야의 기록이다. 제20년 기슬르 월에 나는 수산 성채에 있었다.
ko.R: 이것은 하가랴의 아들 느헤미야의 기록이다. 아닥사스다 왕이 다스린 지 20년째 되던 해 기슬르 월에, 나는 수산 왕궁에 있었다.

pt.L: As palavras de Neemias, filho de Hacalias. E aconteceu, no mês de Quisleu, no ano vigésimo, [que] eu estava em Susã, a cidadela.
pt.B: Relato de Neemias, filho de Hacalias. No mês de Quisleu, no vigésimo ano, eu estava em Susã, a cidadela.
pt.R: Este é o relato de Neemias, filho de Hacalias. No mês de Quisleu, no vigésimo ano do reinado do rei Artaxerxes, eu estava em Susã, na fortaleza real.

decisions.choice: the words of Nehemiah: the account Nehemiah gives, the heading of the book
decisions.reason: The same opening heads the books of Jeremiah and Amos (Jeremiah 1:1; Amos 1:1). Much of what follows is Nehemiah's own first-person account (chapters 1-7 and 12:31-13:31), so the heading names him as its source.

decisions.choice: Kislev in the twentieth year: the ninth month, about November-December, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes
decisions.reason: Kislev is the Babylonian name of the ninth month, used by the Jews after the exile (Zechariah 7:1). The year is counted from the reign of Artaxerxes, named in 2:1; Artaxerxes I ruled Persia from 465 to 424 BC, so this is 445 BC. Nisan, the first month, comes later in the same twentieth year (2:1), which suggests the years of the reign were counted from the autumn.

decisions.choice: Susa the citadel: the fortified royal city of Susa, a residence of the Persian kings
decisions.reason: Susa, in what is now southwest Iran, was one of the capitals of the Persian kings, where they spent the winter. The word for "citadel" names a fortress or palace complex, as in Esther 1:2 and Daniel 8:2.

decisions.choice: the twentieth year that King Artaxerxes ruled
decisions.reason: Readable names the king now, from 2:1, so the reader knows whose reign the year counts.

decisions.choice: "Nehemías hijo de Hacalías", "Quisleu"; "Susa la ciudadela" (L), "la ciudadela de Susa" (B), "la fortaleza real de Susa" (R)
decisions.reason: The names and month in the forms settled for Nehemiah and Esther, Nehemías as already published. Susa's citadel takes the same three wordings here as in Esther 1:2, so the reader meets one place.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah's memoir in the first person ("yo") and the preterite at every level
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-7 are Nehemiah's own account; Spanish keeps "yo" and the narrative preterite throughout, as Ezra's memoir does (Ezra 7:27-9:15).

decisions.choice: Nehemiah's memoir in "je": passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je pris"), passé composé at Readable ("j'ai pris"); speech in the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: The French narrative rule for the whole book, as in Ezra's memoir: written narrative takes the passé simple, Readable the passé composé. Prayers and speeches use present, future and passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "Néhémie fils de Hakalia"; "Suse la citadelle" (L), "la citadelle de Suse" (B), "la forteresse royale de Suse" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms settled for Nehemiah and Esther; Susa's citadel reads the same here as in Esther 1:2.

decisions.choice: "Nehemia mwana wa Hakalia", "Kislevu"; "Shushani ngomeni" (L), "ngome ya Shushani" (B), "ngome ya kifalme huko Shushani" (R)
decisions.reason: "Shushani" is the form already published (Ezra 4:9); the citadel takes the wordings settled for Esther, so both books name the place alike.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah narrates in the first person at every level, with -li- then -ka- in the narrative
decisions.reason: The memoir keeps "mimi" (in the verb) at every level, as Ezra's does; Swahili narrative tenses as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah narrates as "tôi" at every level; one set of address forms through the book
decisions.reason: As Ezra's memoir: a plain "tôi" for the narrator. In speech, through the book: before the king Nehemiah says "vua" (L), "bệ hạ" (B), "đức vua" (R) and calls himself "đầy tớ" (L, B) or "tôi" (R), and the king says "ta" and "ngươi" (2:2-8); to the nobles and officials he says "các ông" (5:7-11; 13:11, 17); to the people "anh em", with the inclusive "chúng ta" (2:17); to nobles and people together he uses no second-person pronoun but the reflexive "mình" (4:8, 13-14); to the foreign traders and to the men he punishes, "ta" and "các người" (13:21, 25-27); Sanballat and he say "ông" each way (2:19-20; 6:2-8); those below him say "ông" to him. In prayer he is "con" before God (1:5).

decisions.choice: "Nê-hê-mi con trai Ha-ca-lia", "tháng Kít-lêu"; "thành nội Su-sơ" (L, B), "hoàng thành Su-sơ" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms settled for Nehemiah and Esther; "Su-sơ" as published (Ezra 4:9), and the citadel worded as in Esther 1:2.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah's memoir in "나" and the plain written style (했다) at every level; one set of speech levels through the book
decisions.reason: As Ezra's memoir. Speech inside it follows the hearer, through the book: before the king 합쇼체 with "임금님" and "이 종" (L, B) or "저" (R), and the king 해라체 with "너" (2:2-8); to the nobles and officials, and to the officials he appoints (7:3), 하오체 with "그대들" (5:7-11; 13:11, 17); to the people 해라체 with "너희" at Literal and Balanced and 합쇼체 with "여러분" at Readable (2:17; 4:8, 13-16), and other leaders speaking to the people the same (8:9-11); to the foreign traders and the men he punishes, 해라체 with "너희" at every level (13:21, 25-27); Sanballat and he 하오체 each way (2:19-20; 6:2-8); those below him 합쇼체, with a title for "you" (6:10). In prayer 합쇼체 with "저/제", "저희" and "주님" (1:5).

decisions.choice: "하가랴의 아들 느헤미야", "기슬르 월", "제20년"; "수산 성" (L), "수산 성채" (B), "수산 왕궁" (R)
decisions.reason: The names in their settled forms, the month with a space as Ezra 6:15, the year in figures as Ezra 7:7; Susa's citadel as in Esther 1:2.

decisions.choice: Neemias, filho de Hacalias; Susã, a cidadela (L, B); Susã, na fortaleza real (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "Neemias" and "Hacalias" are the usual Brazilian forms of the names, with the final -s Portuguese gives to names in -iah, as Isaías and Jeremias. "Susã" is the Portuguese form of the Persian royal city (m3); "a cidadela" keeps the Hebrew apposition at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says what the word names, the king's fortified palace, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: o mês de Quisleu
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the Babylonian month names (m2) are written as names with a capital, as 1 Kings 6:1 and 8:2 do in Portuguese for Zive and Etanim: Quisleu here, Nisã in 2:1, Elul in 6:15. Readable keeps them as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א חֲנָ֜נִי אֶחָ֧ד מֵאַחַ֛י ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁאָלֵ֞ם עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֧ים הַפְּלֵיטָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־נִשְׁאֲר֥וּ מִן־הַשֶּׁ֖בִי וְעַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Hanani, one of my brothers, he and men from Judah, and I asked them about the Jews, the escaped who remained from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

en.L: And Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and some men from Judah. And I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, who had survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
en.B: Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, those who had survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
en.R: Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them how the Jews there were doing, the ones who had survived the exile. I also asked them about Jerusalem.

es.L: Y vino Hananí, uno de mis hermanos, él y [algunos] hombres de Judá, y les pregunté por los judíos que habían escapado, los que habían quedado de la cautividad, y por Jerusalén.
es.B: Hananí, uno de mis hermanos, vino con algunos hombres de Judá. Les pregunté por los judíos que habían escapado, los que habían sobrevivido a la cautividad, y por Jerusalén.
es.R: Hananí, uno de mis hermanos, llegó con algunos hombres de Judá. Les pregunté cómo estaban los judíos de allá, los que habían sobrevivido al destierro. También les pregunté por Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et Hanani, l’un de mes frères, vint, lui et des hommes de Juda. Et je les interrogeai sur les Juifs rescapés, ceux qui étaient restés de la captivité, et sur Jérusalem.
fr.B: Hanani, l’un de mes frères, arriva avec quelques hommes de Juda. Je les interrogeai sur les Juifs rescapés, ceux qui avaient survécu à la captivité, et sur Jérusalem.
fr.R: Hanani, l’un de mes frères, est arrivé avec quelques hommes de Juda. Je leur ai demandé comment allaient les Juifs de là-bas, ceux qui avaient survécu à l’exil. Je leur ai aussi demandé des nouvelles de Jérusalem.

sw.L: Akaja Hanani, mmoja wa ndugu zangu, yeye na watu kutoka Yuda, nami nikawauliza habari za Wayahudi waliookoka, waliosalia kutoka utumwani, na habari za Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Hanani, mmoja wa ndugu zangu, alikuja pamoja na watu kadhaa kutoka Yuda. Nikawauliza habari za Wayahudi waliookoka, wale walionusurika utumwani, na habari za Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Hanani, mmoja wa ndugu zangu, alikuja pamoja na watu kadhaa kutoka Yuda. Niliwauliza hali ya Wayahudi wa huko, wale walionusurika uhamishoni. Niliwauliza pia habari za Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Và Ha-na-ni, một trong các anh em tôi, đến, ông cùng mấy người từ Giu-đa. Và tôi hỏi họ về những người Do Thái đã thoát nạn, những người còn sót lại từ cảnh tù đày, và về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Ha-na-ni, một người anh em của tôi, đến cùng với mấy người từ Giu-đa. Tôi hỏi họ về những người Do Thái đã thoát nạn, tức những người còn sống sót sau cảnh tù đày, và về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Ha-na-ni, một người anh em của tôi, cùng mấy người khác từ Giu-đa đến. Tôi hỏi họ xem những người Do Thái ở đó, những người đã sống sót sau cuộc lưu đày, đang sống ra sao. Tôi cũng hỏi họ về Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 내 형제들 가운데 하나인 하나니가, 그와 유다에서 온 사람들이 왔다. 그래서 나는 그들에게 피하여 남은 유대인들, 곧 포로 생활에서 남은 자들과 예루살렘에 대하여 물었다.
ko.B: 내 형제 가운데 하나인 하나니가 유다에서 온 몇 사람과 함께 왔다. 나는 그들에게 피하여 살아남은 유대인들, 곧 포로 생활에서 살아남은 이들과 예루살렘에 대하여 물었다.
ko.R: 내 형제 하나니가 유다에서 온 몇 사람과 함께 찾아왔다. 나는 그들에게 포로 생활에서 살아남아 그곳에 사는 유대인들이 어떻게 지내는지 물었다. 예루살렘에 대해서도 물었다.

pt.L: E veio Hanani, um dos meus irmãos, ele e [alguns] homens de Judá; e eu lhes perguntei sobre os judeus, os que escaparam, que restaram do cativeiro, e sobre Jerusalém.
pt.B: Hanani, um dos meus irmãos, chegou com alguns homens de Judá. Eu lhes perguntei pelos judeus que tinham escapado, os que tinham sobrevivido ao cativeiro, e por Jerusalém.
pt.R: Hanani, um dos meus irmãos, chegou com alguns homens de Judá. Perguntei a eles como estavam os judeus de lá, os que tinham sobrevivido ao exílio. Também perguntei sobre Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: one of my brothers: Hanani is most likely Nehemiah's own brother
decisions.reason: The word can mean a relative or a fellow Jew, but in 7:2 Nehemiah calls Hanani "my brother", which points to a brother by birth.

decisions.choice: the escaped who remained from the captivity: the Jews who had survived the exile and now lived in Judah
decisions.reason: The two words, "the escaped" and "who remained", are the language of a remnant that came through a disaster alive (Ezra 9:8, 13-15). Here they name the Jewish community in Judah after the Babylonian captivity, most of them people who had returned from it (Ezra 1-2).

decisions.choice: the exile
decisions.reason: Readable says "exile", the common word for the time when the people were taken away to Babylon.

decisions.choice: "anh em" for "brothers"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether a brother is older or younger; the Hebrew does not, so "anh em" keeps it open, and 7:2 "anh em tôi" stays the same.

decisions.choice: o cativeiro (L, B); o exílio (R)
decisions.reason: The word here is the captivity itself (m2), so Literal and Balanced say "cativeiro" and Readable "exílio", as the English Readable says "exile". "Os exilados" is kept, as in Ezra in Portuguese, for the community of those who came back, a different Hebrew phrase.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לִי֒ הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִ֞ים אֲשֶֽׁר־נִשְׁאֲר֤וּ מִן־הַשְּׁבִי֙ שָׁ֣ם בַּמְּדִינָ֔ה בְּרָעָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה וּבְחֶרְפָּ֑ה וְחוֹמַ֤ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ מְפֹרָ֔צֶת וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ נִצְּת֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to me, the remaining who remained from the captivity there in the province [are] in great trouble and in disgrace, and [the] wall of Jerusalem [is] broken down and its gates have been burned with fire.

en.L: And they said to me, "The remnant who survived the captivity there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace, and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
en.B: They said to me, "The survivors of the captivity who are there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned."
en.R: They told me, "The people who survived the exile and are back in the province of Judah are in serious trouble. Others treat them with scorn. The wall of Jerusalem has been broken down, and its gates have been burned."

es.L: Y me dijeron: «Los que quedan, los que quedaron de la cautividad allí en la provincia, están en gran aflicción y en oprobio, y el muro de Jerusalén está derribado, y sus puertas han sido quemadas a fuego».
es.B: Me dijeron: «Los sobrevivientes de la cautividad que están allí en la provincia se encuentran en gran aflicción y deshonra. El muro de Jerusalén está derribado, y sus puertas han sido quemadas».
es.R: Me contaron: «Los que sobrevivieron al destierro y han vuelto a la provincia de Judá están en serios problemas. Los demás los tratan con desprecio. El muro de Jerusalén ha sido derribado, y sus puertas fueron quemadas».

fr.L: Et ils me dirent : « Les restants, ceux qui sont restés de la captivité, là-bas dans la province, sont dans un grand malheur et dans l’opprobre, et la muraille de Jérusalem est abattue, et ses portes ont été brûlées par le feu. »
fr.B: Ils me dirent : « Les rescapés de la captivité qui sont là-bas, dans la province, sont dans un grand malheur et dans la honte. La muraille de Jérusalem est abattue, et ses portes ont été brûlées. »
fr.R: Ils m’ont raconté : « Les gens qui ont survécu à l’exil et qui sont revenus dans la province de Juda ont de graves problèmes. Les autres les traitent avec mépris. La muraille de Jérusalem a été démolie, et ses portes ont été brûlées. »

sw.L: Wakaniambia, "Mabaki waliosalia kutoka utumwani huko katika jimbo wako katika taabu kubwa na katika aibu, na ukuta wa Yerusalemu umebomolewa, na malango yake yamechomwa kwa moto."
sw.B: Wakaniambia, "Walionusurika utumwani walioko huko katika jimbo wako katika taabu kubwa na aibu. Ukuta wa Yerusalemu umebomolewa, na malango yake yamechomwa moto."
sw.R: Waliniambia, "Watu walionusurika uhamishoni na kurudi katika jimbo la Yuda wako katika shida kubwa. Watu wengine wanawadharau. Ukuta wa Yerusalemu umebomolewa, na malango yake yamechomwa moto."

vi.L: Và họ nói với tôi: "Những người còn lại, những người đã sót lại từ cảnh tù đày ở đó trong tỉnh, đang ở trong cảnh khốn khổ lớn và nhục nhã, và tường thành Giê-ru-sa-lem bị phá đổ, và các cổng thành đã bị lửa thiêu đốt."
vi.B: Họ nói với tôi: "Những người sống sót sau cảnh tù đày, hiện ở trong tỉnh ấy, đang gặp hoạn nạn lớn và bị sỉ nhục. Tường thành Giê-ru-sa-lem bị phá đổ, và các cổng thành đã bị đốt cháy."
vi.R: Họ kể cho tôi: "Những người sống sót sau cuộc lưu đày và đã trở về tỉnh Giu-đa đang gặp khó khăn lớn. Người ta khinh bỉ họ. Tường thành Giê-ru-sa-lem đã bị phá sập, còn các cổng thành thì bị đốt cháy."

ko.L: 그들이 나에게 말했다. "그곳 지방에서 포로 생활에서 남은 자들, 그 남은 자들이 큰 고난과 수치 가운데 있고, 예루살렘 성벽은 무너졌으며, 그 성문들은 불에 탔습니다."
ko.B: 그들이 나에게 말했다. "포로 생활에서 살아남아 그 지방에 있는 사람들이 큰 고난과 수치를 당하고 있습니다. 예루살렘 성벽은 무너졌고, 성문들은 불타 버렸습니다."
ko.R: 그들이 나에게 이렇게 전했다. "포로 생활에서 살아남아 유다 지방으로 돌아온 사람들이 큰 어려움을 겪고 있습니다. 다른 사람들이 그들을 업신여깁니다. 예루살렘 성벽은 허물어졌고, 성문들은 불에 타 버렸습니다."

pt.L: E eles me disseram: "Os que restaram, que sobreviveram ao cativeiro, ali na província, [estão] em grande aflição e em opróbrio; e o muro de Jerusalém [está] derrubado, e as suas portas foram queimadas a fogo."
pt.B: Eles me disseram: "Os sobreviventes do cativeiro que estão lá na província passam por grande aflição e humilhação. O muro de Jerusalém está derrubado, e as suas portas foram queimadas."
pt.R: Eles me contaram: "As pessoas que sobreviveram ao exílio e voltaram para a província de Judá estão passando por muitas dificuldades. Os outros povos as tratam com desprezo. O muro de Jerusalém foi derrubado, e as suas portas foram queimadas."

decisions.choice: the province: Judah, a small province of the Persian empire
decisions.reason: After the exile Judah was governed as a province of the Persian empire (Ezra 2:1; 5:8), part of the larger region Beyond the River (2:7).

decisions.choice: the wall broken down and the gates burned: Jerusalem lay without defenses
decisions.reason: The Babylonians broke down Jerusalem's walls and burned the city in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9-10). The news may also include a more recent setback: under this same Artaxerxes the Jews' work on the walls had been stopped by force (Ezra 4:12, 21-23). The text does not say which; either way the city could not be defended.

decisions.choice: disgrace: open shame, being mocked by others
decisions.reason: The word means reproach or scorn from others. A city without walls was a mark of weakness and of God's judgment, and the neighbors mock it (2:17, 19; 3:33-36).

decisions.choice: the province of Judah; Others treat them with scorn
decisions.reason: Readable names the province and says who causes the disgrace, so the reader sees it is shame before others.

decisions.choice: "el muro de Jerusalén" for the city wall, through the book
decisions.reason: The wall Nehemiah rebuilds is "el muro", the word the gate list uses ("el Muro Ancho", 3:8), so the wall and its named sections share one word.

decisions.choice: "la muraille" for the city wall, through the book
decisions.reason: The wall of a city is "la muraille", as the terms note sets; "mur" is kept for the wall of a house.

decisions.choice: The men from Judah speak to Nehemiah in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: They report to a high official of the Persian court, so their words take the formal polite style; the narration around them stays plain.

decisions.choice: o muro; as portas
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "o muro" for the city wall (m2) and "as portas" for its gates, the words Portuguese Bibles have long used for Jerusalem's wall and its named gates (chapter 3: "a Porta das Ovelhas", "a Porta do Vale"). "Muralha" would also do but is kept out so that one word runs through the building story.

decisions.choice: opróbrio (L); humilhação (B); R as the English
decisions.reason: "Opróbrio" is the shame of being reproached by others (m3); Balanced says "humilhação", the plain word for public disgrace, and Readable says who causes it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כְּשָׁמְעִ֣י׀אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה יָשַׁ֨בְתִּי֙ וָֽאֶבְכֶּ֔ה וָאֶתְאַבְּלָ֖ה יָמִ֑ים וָֽאֱהִ֥י צָם֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when I heard the words, these, I sat and wept and mourned days, and I was fasting and praying before [the] God of the heavens.

en.L: And when I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
en.B: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. For some days I mourned, and I kept fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
en.R: When I heard this news, I sat down and cried. For several days I was full of grief. I went without food, and I prayed to the God of heaven.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando oí estas palabras, me senté y lloré e hice duelo por días, y estuve ayunando y orando delante del Dios de los cielos.
es.B: Cuando oí estas palabras, me senté y lloré. Durante algunos días hice duelo, y seguí ayunando y orando delante del Dios de los cielos.
es.R: Cuando oí estas noticias, me senté y lloré. Durante varios días estuve muy triste. Dejé de comer, y oré al Dios de los cielos.

fr.L: Et quand j’entendis ces paroles, je m’assis et je pleurai, et je fus dans le deuil pendant des jours, et je jeûnais et je priais devant le Dieu des cieux.
fr.B: Quand j’entendis ces paroles, je m’assis et je pleurai. Pendant quelques jours, je fus dans le deuil, et je ne cessai de jeûner et de prier devant le Dieu des cieux.
fr.R: Quand j’ai entendu ces nouvelles, je me suis assis et j’ai pleuré. Pendant plusieurs jours, j’ai été plein de tristesse. Je n’ai pas mangé, et j’ai prié le Dieu du ciel.

sw.L: Ikawa niliposikia maneno haya, niliketi, nikalia, nikaomboleza kwa siku, nami nilikuwa nikifunga na kuomba mbele ya Mungu wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Niliposikia maneno haya, niliketi chini, nikalia. Kwa siku kadhaa niliomboleza, nikaendelea kufunga na kuomba mbele ya Mungu wa mbinguni.
sw.R: Niliposikia habari hizi, niliketi chini, nikalia. Kwa siku kadhaa nilikuwa na huzuni kubwa. Sikula chakula, nikamwomba Mungu wa mbinguni.

vi.L: Và khi tôi nghe những lời này, tôi ngồi xuống và khóc, và than khóc nhiều ngày, và tôi kiêng ăn và cầu nguyện trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời trên trời.
vi.B: Khi nghe những lời ấy, tôi ngồi xuống mà khóc. Suốt mấy ngày tôi than khóc, và tôi cứ kiêng ăn, cầu nguyện trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời trên trời.
vi.R: Khi nghe tin ấy, tôi ngồi xuống và khóc. Suốt mấy ngày tôi rất đau buồn. Tôi nhịn ăn và cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời trên trời.

ko.L: 내가 이 말들을 들었을 때에, 나는 주저앉아 울었고, 여러 날 슬퍼하며, 하늘의 하나님 앞에서 금식하며 기도했다.
ko.B: 이 말을 듣고 나는 주저앉아 울었다. 며칠 동안 슬퍼하며, 하늘의 하나님 앞에서 계속 금식하고 기도했다.
ko.R: 이 소식을 듣고 나는 주저앉아 울었다. 여러 날 동안 몹시 슬퍼했다. 나는 음식을 먹지 않고 하늘의 하나님께 기도했다.

pt.L: E, quando ouvi estas palavras, sentei-me, e chorei, e fiquei de luto [por alguns] dias, e estive jejuando e orando diante do Deus dos céus.
pt.B: Quando ouvi essas palavras, sentei-me e chorei. Durante alguns dias fiquei de luto, e continuei jejuando e orando diante do Deus dos céus.
pt.R: Quando ouvi essas notícias, eu me sentei e chorei. Durante vários dias fiquei muito triste. Fiquei sem comer e orei ao Deus dos céus.

decisions.choice: sat, wept, mourned, fasted: the signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: Sitting on the ground, weeping and fasting were how grief and repentance were shown (Ezra 9:3-5; 10:6; Job 2:13). Nehemiah's prayer that follows is also a confession (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: days: for a number of days
decisions.reason: The plural without a number means "some days". From Kislev (1:1) to Nisan (2:1) is about four months, and the prayer may have gone on through that time (verse 6, "day and night").

decisions.choice: the God of heaven: a title of God common in the Persian period
decisions.reason: The title is used in Cyrus's decree and in the Persian letters (Ezra 1:2; 7:12), and by Nehemiah in his prayers and speech (1:5; 2:4, 20). It names the God of Israel as the God over all.

decisions.choice: "el Dios de los cielos" at every level
decisions.reason: The title as Ezra renders it in Spanish (Ezra 1:2), kept the same through Nehemiah.

decisions.choice: "le Dieu des cieux" (L, B), "le Dieu du ciel" (R)
decisions.reason: The title in Ezra's French wording, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "Mungu wa mbinguni" at every level
decisions.reason: The title as Ezra's Swahili gives it, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời trên trời" at every level
alternatives: Đức Chúa Trời của các tầng trời
decisions.reason: The title as Ezra's Vietnamese gives it, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "하늘의 하나님" at every level
decisions.reason: The title as Ezra's Korean gives it, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: o Deus dos céus
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the title (m3) keeps the Hebrew plural "céus" at every level, as Ezra 7:12 does in Portuguese; it is the form Portuguese has always used for this title.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר אָֽנָּ֤א יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם הָאֵ֥ל הַגָּד֖וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָ֑א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וָחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, please, YHWH, God of the heavens, the God, the great and the awesome, keeping the covenant and steadfast love for those loving him and for those keeping his commandments,

en.L: And I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of the heavens, the great and awesome God, keeping the covenant and steadfast love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,
en.B: And I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and faithful love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,
en.R: I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of heaven, great and awesome God! You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love to those who love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

es.L: Y dije: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los cielos, Dios grande y temible, que guarda el pacto y el amor leal con los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman y guardan {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos,
es.B: Y dije: «Te lo ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los cielos, el Dios grande y temible, que guarda el pacto y el amor fiel con los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman y cumplen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos,
es.R: Dije: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los cielos, ¡Dios grande y temible! Tú cumples {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto y muestras amor fiel a los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} aman y obedecen {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} mandamientos.

fr.L: Et je dis : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des cieux, Dieu grand et redoutable, qui garde l’alliance et l’amour fidèle envers ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aiment et qui gardent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements,
fr.B: Je dis : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des cieux, le Dieu grand et redoutable, qui garde l’alliance et l’amour fidèle envers ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aiment et observent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements,
fr.R: J’ai dit : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu du ciel, Dieu grand et redoutable ! Tu restes fidèle à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montres {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour fidèle à ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}aiment et qui obéissent à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} commandements.

sw.L: Nikasema, "Nakusihi, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, Mungu mkuu na wa kuogofya, unayeshika agano na upendo usiokoma kwa wale wanaokupenda na kuzishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}},
sw.B: Nikasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, nakusihi! Wewe ni Mungu mkuu na wa kuogofya, unayeshika agano na upendo usiokoma pamoja na wale wanaokupenda na kuzitii amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}},
sw.R: Nilisema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, nakuomba! Wewe ni Mungu mkuu na wa kuogofya. Unashika agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} na kuwaonyesha upendo usiokoma wale wanaokupenda na kuzitii amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}.

vi.L: Và tôi thưa: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời trên trời, Đức Chúa Trời vĩ đại và đáng kính sợ, Đấng giữ giao ước và tình yêu thương thành tín với những người yêu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},
vi.B: Tôi thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời trên trời, con nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}! Ngài là Đức Chúa Trời vĩ đại và đáng kính sợ, Đấng giữ giao ước và tình yêu thương thành tín với những người yêu mến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và vâng giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},
vi.R: Tôi thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời trên trời, con nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}! Ngài là Đức Chúa Trời vĩ đại và đáng kính sợ. Ngài giữ giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và tỏ tình thương không hề thay đổi với những người yêu mến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và vâng theo các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 말했다. "아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 하늘의 하나님, 크고 두려우신 하나님, 주님을 사랑하고 주님의 계명들을 지키는 자들에게 언약과 한결같은 사랑을 지키시는 분이시여,
ko.B: 내가 아뢰었다. "하늘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 크고 두려우신 하나님, 주님을 사랑하고 주님의 계명을 지키는 사람들에게 언약과 한결같은 사랑을 지키시는 분이시여, 간구합니다.
ko.R: 나는 이렇게 아뢰었다. "하늘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 간절히 구합니다. 주님은 크고 두려우신 하나님이십니다. 주님은 언약을 지키시고, 주님을 사랑하며 주님의 계명을 따르는 사람들에게 변함없는 사랑을 베푸십니다.

pt.L: E eu disse: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus dos céus, o grande e temível Deus, que guarda a aliança e o amor leal para com os que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} amam e guardam os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} mandamentos,
pt.B: Eu disse: "Peço-te, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus dos céus, o grande e temível Deus, que guarda a aliança e o amor leal para com os que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} amam e obedecem aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} mandamentos,
pt.R: Eu disse: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus dos céus! Tu és o grande e temível Deus. Tu guardas a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} aliança e mostras amor leal aos que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amam e obedecem aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} mandamentos.

decisions.choice: the great and awesome God who keeps the covenant and steadfast love: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The prayer opens with Moses' words in Deuteronomy 7:9, 21 ("the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments"), as Daniel's prayer does (Daniel 9:4). Nehemiah appeals to what God has already said about himself.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal, lasting love that keeps faith with a covenant
decisions.reason: The word means kindness that is owed and freely kept, the love that holds to a relationship. Here it is joined to "covenant", the bond God made with Israel.

decisions.choice: awesome: to be feared, inspiring awe
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to fear". It describes God as one to be held in awe and reverence (Deuteronomy 7:21; 10:17).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the project, Literal says "steadfast love" and Balanced and Readable "faithful love".

decisions.choice: You keep your covenant ... those who love you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the description into a sentence spoken to God, as the prayer goes on to speak to him directly.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} in address, with no "oh"; elsewhere "el SEÑOR", "del SEÑOR", "al SEÑOR"
decisions.reason: The divine name in the Spanish form used through the Old Testament, for the whole book; the alternative gives the name as most scholars think it was said, as the English "Yahweh" does. God is addressed as "tú", with the deity_pronoun setting on his free pronouns.

decisions.choice: "Dios grande y temible, que guarda el pacto y el amor leal con los que lo aman" (L); "el amor fiel" (B)
decisions.reason: The words of Deuteronomy 7:9 and 10:17 as already published in Spanish, so the reader hears the quotation; 9:32 repeats them.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} in address, no article and no "ô"; elsewhere "le SEIGNEUR", "du SEIGNEUR", "au SEIGNEUR"
decisions.reason: The divine name as the French Old Testament gives it, for the whole book. God is addressed as "tu", and every pronoun for him takes the deity_pronoun setting, imperatives included ("souviens-toi").

decisions.choice: "Dieu grand et redoutable, qui garde l'alliance et l'amour fidèle envers ceux qui l'aiment"
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 7:9 and 10:17 as published in French, so the quotation is heard; 9:32 repeats it.

decisions.choice: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}" in address; BWANA elsewhere
decisions.reason: The divine name as the Swahili Old Testament gives it, for the whole book. The deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives ("zako", "lako", "kwako"), never on verb prefixes.

decisions.choice: "Mungu mkuu na wa kuogofya, unayeshika agano na upendo usiokoma"
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 7:9 and 10:17 with God's steadfast love as "upendo usiokoma", as the published Psalms and Ezra; 9:32 repeats it.

decisions.choice: "lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}" in address; CHÚA elsewhere, particles outside the span
decisions.reason: The divine name as the Vietnamese Old Testament gives it, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: In prayer Nehemiah calls himself "con", the people "chúng con", and God "Ngài" or "Chúa"
decisions.reason: The forms of Ezra's prayer (Ezra 9:6) and the Psalms; his narration stays "tôi". "Ngài" in mid-sentence carries the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" in address, particles outside the span; no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The divine name as the Korean Old Testament gives it, for the whole book. Korean has no capitals, so respect for God is carried by the honorific -시- and 주님, not by a setting.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah prays in 합쇼체, with "저"/"제" for himself, "저희" for the people and "주님" for "you"
decisions.reason: As Ezra's prayer (Ezra 9:6, 15) and the Psalms. The formula of Deuteronomy 7:9 keeps its published words, "크고 두려우신 하나님" and "한결같은 사랑" ("변함없는 사랑" at Readable).

decisions.choice: tu, with deity_pronoun spans (1:5-11 and every prayer of the book); SENHOR without the article in the vocative
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Nehemiah speaks to God with "tu", as every prayer does in Portuguese (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), every pronoun for God under the deity_pronoun span, and the name in the vocative without its article, as Solomon's prayer in 1 Kings 8:23. Where the Hebrew speaks of God in the third person (here, "those who love him") Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable turns it to "tu", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: o grande e temível Deus, que guarda a aliança e o amor leal
decisions.reason: The prayer opens with Moses' words (m1), so it keeps the wording of Deuteronomy 7:9 and 7:21 in Portuguese: "temível" for the God to be held in awe (m3), "guarda a aliança e o amor leal" for God's covenant love (m2), "amor leal" at every level as the Old Testament terms set it. decisions.choice: let your ear be attentive and your eyes open: please listen and take notice
decisions.reason: Ear and eyes picture God paying attention to the one who prays, as in Solomon's prayer at the temple (1 Kings 8:29, 52; 2 Chronicles 6:40).

decisions.choice: today, day and night: the prayer he prays now, and has kept praying without stopping
decisions.reason: "Today" points to the prayer he is speaking; "day and night" says he has prayed this way continually, through the days of verse 4.

decisions.choice: confessing the sins of Israel, including his own and his family's
decisions.reason: Nehemiah does not blame others only: he counts himself and his family among those who sinned, as Ezra and Daniel do in their prayers (Ezra 9:6-7; Daniel 9:5-8, 20).

decisions.choice: your slave, your slaves: one who belongs to God and serves him
decisions.reason: Calling oneself God's slave or servant is the humble language of prayer (1 Samuel 3:9-10; 1 Kings 8:28). It speaks of belonging to God and being bound to obey him.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word: Literal keeps "slave", Balanced and Readable say "servant", since the point here is belonging and service, not slavery itself.

decisions.choice: my father's family (Balanced); my own family (Readable)
decisions.reason: "House of my father" means one's family or clan. Balanced and Readable say "family", as the project does for this phrase.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L), "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" and "israelitas" already include women and men, so the English gender setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: "esclavo" (L); "siervo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain word for a slave, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say "siervo", the word of humble prayer.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the word for a slave, Balanced and Readable the servant of humble prayer. "con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên" and "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" already include women and men, so no gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: "종" at every level; "이 종" (B) for Nehemiah himself
decisions.reason: "종" is both slave and servant in Korean prayer, so one word serves every level; "이스라엘 자손" already includes women and men.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender span
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms and Ezra 7:7 in Portuguese: "filhos" and "israelitas" already include women and men, so Portuguese has no second wording to offer where the English has a gender span. The same throughout the book.

decisions.choice: o teu ouvido atento e os teus olhos abertos (L, B); escuta com atenção e olha (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Solomon's prayer (m1), with "olhos abertos" and "atento" as 2 Chronicles 6:40 in Portuguese; Nehemiah's "ear" is singular, and Literal and Balanced keep it so. Readable says what the picture asks, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: corruptly we have acted corruptly: we have acted very corruptly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled (an infinitive before the finite verb), which makes it emphatic. The verb means to act in a ruinous, destructive way.

decisions.choice: the commandments, the statutes and the judgments: the whole law given through Moses
decisions.reason: The three words together name all that God commanded in the law (Deuteronomy 5:31; 6:1). Israel's failure to keep it is why the exile came (Deuteronomy 28:15, 64).

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes, judgments (Literal); commandments, statutes, rulings (Balanced); commands, laws, rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's settled wording for these three words of the law.

decisions.reason: The three words of the law as Deuteronomy 6:1 renders them in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "commandements, prescriptions, jugements" (L); "commandements, prescriptions, règles" (B); "commandements, lois, règles" (R)
decisions.reason: The three words of the law as Deuteronomy 6:1 renders them in French.

decisions.reason: The three words of the law as Deuteronomy 6:1 renders them in Swahili.

records.literal_gloss: Remember, please, the word which you commanded Moses your slave, saying, you, you will act unfaithfully, I, I will scatter you among the peoples;

en.L: Remember, please, the word which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples.
en.B: Please remember the word that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations.
en.R: Please remember what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses. You said, 'If you are not faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will scatter you among the nations.

es.L: Acuérdate, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego, de la palabra que mandaste a Moisés, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} esclavo, diciendo: “Si {{plural_you:ustedes actúan|vosotros actuáis}} con infidelidad, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} dispersaré entre los pueblos.
es.B: Te ruego que recuerdes la palabra que diste a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo Moisés: “Si {{plural_you:ustedes son infieles|vosotros sois infieles}}, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} dispersaré entre las naciones.
es.R: Por favor, recuerda lo que le dijiste a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo Moisés. Le dijiste: “Si {{plural_you:ustedes no son|vosotros no sois}} fieles a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} dispersaré entre las naciones.

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, de grâce, de la parole que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as commandée à Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} esclave, en disant : “Si vous êtes infidèles, je vous disperserai parmi les peuples.
fr.B: De grâce, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de la parole que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as donnée à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur Moïse : “Si vous êtes infidèles, je vous disperserai parmi les nations.
fr.R: De grâce, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur Moïse. Tu as dit : “Si vous n’êtes pas fidèles envers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous disperserai parmi les nations.

sw.L: Ukumbuke, tafadhali, neno ulilomwamuru Musa mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, ukisema, 'Ninyi mkikosa uaminifu, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitawatawanya kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Tafadhali ukumbuke neno ulilompa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Musa: 'Mkikosa uaminifu, nitawatawanya katika mataifa.
sw.R: Tafadhali ukumbuke ulichomwambia mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Musa. Ulisema, 'Msipokuwa waaminifu {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, nitawatawanya katika mataifa.

vi.L: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại lời mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền cho Môi-se, nô lệ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rằng: 'Các ngươi, nếu các ngươi bất trung, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho các ngươi tản lạc giữa các dân.
vi.B: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán dặn Môi-se, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: 'Nếu các ngươi bất trung, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phân tán các ngươi giữa các dân tộc.
vi.R: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán với Môi-se, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài đã phán: 'Nếu các ngươi không trung thành với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phân tán các ngươi giữa các dân tộc.

ko.L: 부디 주님께서 주님의 종 모세에게 명령하여 말씀하신 것을 기억해 주십시오. '너희가 신실하지 못하게 행하면, 내가 너희를 민족들 가운데 흩을 것이다.
ko.B: 주님께서 주님의 종 모세에게 주신 말씀을 기억해 주십시오. '너희가 신의를 저버리면 내가 너희를 여러 민족 가운데 흩어 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 주님께서 주님의 종 모세에게 하신 말씀을 기억해 주십시오. 주님께서는 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다. '너희가 나에게 신실하지 않으면, 내가 너희를 여러 나라에 흩어 버릴 것이다.

pt.L: Lembra-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}, por favor, da palavra que ordenaste a Moisés, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} escravo, dizendo: 'Se vocês agirem com infidelidade, eu os espalharei entre os povos.
pt.B: Lembra-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}, por favor, da palavra que deste ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo Moisés: 'Se vocês forem infiéis, eu os espalharei entre as nações.
pt.R: Por favor, lembra-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} do que disseste ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo Moisés. Tu disseste: 'Se vocês não forem fiéis a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, eu vou espalhar vocês entre as nações.

decisions.choice: the word to Moses: a summary of the warnings and promises of the law
decisions.reason: Nehemiah does not quote one verse but sums up what God said through Moses: unfaithfulness would bring scattering among the nations (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 4:25-27; 28:64), and turning back would bring gathering (verse 9).

decisions.choice: you will act unfaithfully, I will scatter you: if you are unfaithful, I will scatter you
decisions.reason: The two clauses stand side by side with no "if", but the first states a condition and the second its result, as verse 9 goes on with "and if you return". The pronouns "you" and "I" are written out for emphasis.

decisions.choice: act unfaithfully: break faith, betray a trust
decisions.reason: The verb means to be disloyal to one to whom loyalty is owed, often of turning from God (Leviticus 26:40; Ezra 9:2, 4).

decisions.choice: nations
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "nations", the sense of "peoples" here, foreign peoples outside Israel.

decisions.choice: not faithful to me
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the faithfulness was owed, which the verb implies.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} on every plural "you", verbs and pronouns too, for the whole book
decisions.reason: God's word through Moses speaks to all Israel, so it is plural; Spanish gives the Latin American "ustedes" by default and the "vosotros" of Spain as the alternative, as through the published Old Testament. God and single persons are "tú".

decisions.choice: God's own free "mimi" (L) and "kwangu" (R) take the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili spans God's free pronouns, his own included, as the Kings drafts do ("langu", 1 Kings 8:29); the English has no span on "I", but Swahili writes the pronoun out only where the Hebrew stresses it.

decisions.choice: God speaking to Israel: "Ta" for himself, "các ngươi" for the people
decisions.reason: God's own words to the people take "Ta" and "các ngươi", as his speeches in the Prophets; "Ta" in mid-sentence carries the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: God's quoted words in 해라체 with "너희" and "나"
decisions.reason: God speaking to his people uses 해라체 and names himself without -시-, as in the Pentateuch; Nehemiah's prayer around the quotation stays in 합쇼체.

decisions.choice: vocês (God to Israel, plural)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" in God's words is plural (m2), Israel as a people, so God says "vocês", as he does to Israel in the plural throughout the Old Testament in Portuguese.

source.text: וְשַׁבְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ מִצְוֺתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אִם־יִהְיֶ֨ה נִֽדַּחֲכֶ֜ם בִּקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִשָּׁ֣ם אֲקַבְּצֵ֔ם וַהֲבִֽיאוֹתִים֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתִּי לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will return to me and keep my commandments and do them, if will be your banished one at [the] end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and I will bring them to the place which I have chosen to make dwell my name there.

en.L: But if you return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and do them, even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place which I have chosen to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name dwell there.'
en.B: But if you return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and obey them, even if your exiles are at the farthest edge of the sky, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'
en.R: But if you come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, I will gather your people again, even if they have been scattered to the farthest places on earth. I will bring them back to the place I chose, where I will be worshiped.'

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:se vuelven|os volvéis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y {{plural_you:guardan|guardáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos y los {{plural_you:cumplen|cumplís}}, aunque {{plural_you:sus desterrados|vuestros desterrados}} estén en el extremo de los cielos, de allí los reuniré y los traeré al lugar que he escogido para hacer habitar allí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre”.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:vuelven|volvéis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y {{plural_you:guardan|guardáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos y los {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} en práctica, aunque {{plural_you:sus desterrados|vuestros desterrados}} estén en el confín más lejano del cielo, yo los reuniré de allí y los traeré al lugar que he escogido como morada para {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre”.
es.R: Pero si {{plural_you:vuelven|volvéis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos, yo volveré a reunir a {{plural_you:su pueblo|vuestro pueblo}}, aunque haya sido dispersado hasta los lugares más lejanos de la tierra. Los traeré de vuelta al lugar que escogí, donde se me adorará”.

fr.L: Mais si vous revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et gardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements et les mettez en pratique, même si vos bannis sont à l’extrémité des cieux, de là je les rassemblerai et je les ferai venir au lieu que j’ai choisi pour y faire demeurer {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.”
fr.B: Mais si vous revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, si vous gardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements et les mettez en pratique, même si vos exilés se trouvent au bout du ciel, je les rassemblerai de là et je les ramènerai au lieu que j’ai choisi pour y faire habiter {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.”
fr.R: Mais si vous revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et obéissez à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, je rassemblerai de nouveau votre peuple, même s’il a été dispersé jusqu’aux endroits les plus lointains de la terre. Je les ramènerai au lieu que j’ai choisi, là où l’on m’adorera.”

sw.L: Lakini mkirudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} na kuzishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kuzitenda, hata kama waliofukuzwa wenu wako katika miisho ya mbingu, kutoka huko nitawakusanya na kuwaleta mahali nilipochagua ili kulifanya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} likae huko.'
sw.B: Lakini mkinirudia na kuzishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kuzitii, hata kama watu wenu waliohamishwa wako kwenye ukingo wa mbali kabisa wa mbingu, nitawakusanya kutoka huko na kuwaleta mahali nilipochagua pawe makao ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.'
sw.R: Lakini mkinirudia na kuzitii amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, nitawakusanya tena watu wenu, hata kama wametawanywa mpaka sehemu za mbali kabisa za dunia. Nitawarudisha mahali nilipochagua, mahali nitakapoabudiwa.'

vi.L: Nhưng nếu các ngươi trở lại với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và làm theo, thì dù những kẻ bị đày của các ngươi ở tận cùng các tầng trời, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ thu nhóm họ từ đó và đem họ đến nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn để cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ngự tại đó.'
vi.B: Nhưng nếu các ngươi quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, giữ và làm theo các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì dù những người lưu đày của các ngươi có ở tận chân trời, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ thu nhóm họ từ đó và đem họ về nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn làm chỗ ngự cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'
vi.R: Nhưng nếu các ngươi quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vâng giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thu nhóm dân các ngươi trở lại, dù họ đã bị phân tán đến những nơi xa nhất trên đất. Ta sẽ đem họ về nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn, là nơi người ta sẽ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'

ko.L: 그러나 너희가 나에게 돌아와 내 계명들을 지키고 그것들을 행하면, 너희 쫓겨난 자들이 하늘 끝에 있을지라도, 내가 거기에서 그들을 모아, 내 이름을 거기에 머물게 하려고 내가 택한 곳으로 그들을 데려올 것이다.'
ko.B: 그러나 너희가 나에게 돌아와 내 계명을 지켜 행하면, 너희 가운데 쫓겨난 사람들이 하늘 저 끝에 있을지라도 내가 거기에서 그들을 모아, 내 이름이 머물 곳으로 택한 곳으로 데려올 것이다.'
ko.R: 그러나 너희가 나에게 돌아와 내 명령을 지키면, 너희 백성이 땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 흩어졌을지라도 내가 그들을 다시 모을 것이다. 그리고 내가 택한 곳, 곧 사람들이 나를 예배할 곳으로 그들을 데려올 것이다.'

pt.L: Mas, se vocês voltarem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e guardarem os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} mandamentos e os praticarem, mesmo que os banidos de vocês estejam na extremidade dos céus, dali eu os reunirei e os trarei ao lugar que escolhi para fazer habitar ali o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome.'
pt.B: Mas, se vocês voltarem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, guardarem os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} mandamentos e os cumprirem, mesmo que os exilados de vocês estejam nos confins do céu, eu os reunirei de lá e os trarei ao lugar que escolhi como habitação para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome.'
pt.R: Mas, se vocês voltarem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e obedecerem aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} mandamentos, eu vou reunir de novo o povo de vocês, mesmo que ele tenha sido espalhado pelos lugares mais distantes da terra. Vou trazer todos de volta ao lugar que escolhi, onde eu serei adorado.'

decisions.choice: if you return ... even at the end of the heavens, I will gather them: Deuteronomy 30:1-4
decisions.reason: This takes up Moses' promise that if the scattered people turn back to God, he will gather them "even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens" (Deuteronomy 30:4).

decisions.choice: the end of the heavens: the farthest horizon, the most distant places
decisions.reason: The sky seems to meet the earth at the horizon, so its "end" is the farthest place one can think of (Deuteronomy 4:32; Psalm 19:7).

decisions.choice: the place I have chosen to make my name dwell: Jerusalem and its temple
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place God would choose "to make his name dwell there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). God's name stands for his presence among his people; the place came to be Jerusalem (1 Kings 8:29; 11:36).

decisions.choice: But if you return
decisions.reason: The "and" that joins this to verse 8 turns the warning into its opposite, so Balanced and Readable say "But" and the "if" that the sense needs.

decisions.choice: where I will be worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for God's name to dwell in a place, since the picture is not plain to a new reader. It is a simplification: the phrase also speaks of God's presence there.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus desterrados|vuestros desterrados}}, the span taking in the noun
decisions.reason: With "ustedes", a bare "sus" could be read as "their"; spanning the whole phrase keeps "your banished ones" plain.

decisions.choice: os banidos ... na extremidade dos céus (L); os confins do céu (B); para fazer habitar ali o meu nome (L), como habitação para o meu nome (B)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah takes up Deuteronomy 30:4 and 12:5, 11 (m1, m3), so each level keeps the Portuguese of those verses: "extremidade dos céus" and "confins do céu" for the farthest horizon, and the formula of the place God chose for his name.

source.text: וְהֵ֥ם עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וְעַמֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּדִ֨יתָ֙ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ הַגָּד֔וֹל וּבְיָדְךָ֖ הַחֲזָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they [are] your slaves and your people, whom you redeemed by your power, the great, and by your hand, the strong.

en.L: And they are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.
en.B: They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.
en.R: They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people. You set them free by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.

es.L: Y ellos son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} esclavos y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, que redimiste con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder y con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano fuerte.
es.B: Ellos son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, a quienes redimiste con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano poderosa.
es.R: Ellos son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propio pueblo. Tú los libertaste con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano fuerte.

fr.L: Et ils sont {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} esclaves et {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as rachetés par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance et par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main forte.
fr.B: Ils sont {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs et {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as rachetés par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main puissante.
fr.R: Ils sont {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} propre peuple. Tu les as libérés par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main forte.

sw.L: Nao ni watumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, uliowakomboa kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kuu na kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye nguvu.
sw.B: Wao ni watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, uliowakomboa kwa uweza {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mkuu na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye nguvu.
sw.R: Wao ni watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Uliwaweka huru kwa uweza {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mkuu na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye nguvu.

vi.L: Và họ là các nô lệ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cứu chuộc bằng quyền năng lớn lao của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và bằng bàn tay mạnh mẽ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ là các đầy tớ và là dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cứu chuộc bằng quyền năng lớn lao và bàn tay mạnh mẽ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Họ là các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là dân riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài đã giải phóng họ bằng quyền năng lớn lao và bàn tay mạnh mẽ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.B: 그들은 주님께서 큰 능력과 강한 손으로 구속하신 주님의 종들이며 주님의 백성입니다.
ko.R: 그들은 주님의 종들이며 주님의 백성입니다. 주님께서 큰 능력과 강한 손으로 그들을 자유롭게 해 주셨습니다.

pt.L: E eles [são] os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} escravos e o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} resgataste com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} grande poder e com a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão forte.
pt.B: Eles são os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} servos e o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} resgataste com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} grande poder e com a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão forte.
pt.R: Eles são os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} servos, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} próprio povo. Tu os libertaste com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} grande poder e com a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão forte.

decisions.choice: your people whom you redeemed by your great power and strong hand: Moses' prayer and the exodus
decisions.reason: Moses prayed in almost these words when Israel had sinned: "they are your people ... whom you brought out by your great power" (Deuteronomy 9:29; Exodus 32:11). The redemption is the rescue from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free, rescued at a price
decisions.reason: The verb means to ransom or set free, used of God bringing Israel out of slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 15:15).

decisions.choice: strong hand: God's power shown in action
decisions.reason: A strong hand pictures power at work; it is a set phrase for the exodus (Exodus 3:19; Deuteronomy 6:21).

decisions.choice: set them free
decisions.reason: Readable says what "redeemed" means here, freedom from slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: resgataste (L, B); libertaste (R)
decisions.reason: "Resgatar" is the verb Exodus 6:6 and Deuteronomy 7:8 use in Portuguese for God's setting Israel free from Egypt (m2); "redimir" readers often hear only as forgiveness.

source.text: אָנָּ֣א אֲדֹנָ֗י תְּהִ֣י נָ֣א אָזְנְךָֽ־קַ֠שֶּׁבֶת אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֜ וְאֶל־תְּפִלַּ֣ת עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽחֲפֵצִים֙ לְיִרְאָ֣ה אֶת־שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וְהַצְלִֽיחָה־נָּ֤א לְעַבְדְּךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וּתְנֵ֣הוּ לְרַחֲמִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַאֲנִ֛י הָיִ֥יתִי מַשְׁקֶ֖ה לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Please, my Lord, let be, please, your ear attentive to [the] prayer of your slave and to [the] prayer of your slaves, the ones delighting to fear your name, and give success, please, to your slave today, and give him compassion before the man, this. And I was cupbearer to the king.

en.L: Please, my Lord, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave and to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves who delight to fear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and give success, please, to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave today, and grant him compassion before this man." And I was cupbearer to the king.
en.B: Please, Lord, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who delight to honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. Give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant success today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man." Now I was cupbearer to the king.
en.R: Please, Lord, listen to my prayer. Listen to the prayers of all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who are glad to honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Help me today, and make the king kind to me." At that time I served the king as his cupbearer.

es.L: Te ruego, Señor mío, que esté atento {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oído a la oración de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} esclavo y a la oración de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} esclavos, que se complacen en temer {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre; y concede éxito, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego, a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} esclavo hoy, y dale compasión delante de este hombre». Y yo era copero del rey.
es.B: Te ruego, Señor, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oído esté atento a la oración de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo y a la oración de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos que se complacen en honrar {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre. Concede hoy éxito a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, y haz que halle misericordia delante de este hombre». Yo era entonces copero del rey.
es.R: Señor, por favor, escucha mi oración. Escucha las oraciones de todos {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos que se alegran de honrarte. Ayúdame hoy, y haz que el rey sea bondadoso conmigo». En ese tiempo yo servía al rey como su copero.

fr.L: De grâce, mon Seigneur, que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} oreille soit attentive à la prière de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} esclave et à la prière de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} esclaves qui prennent plaisir à craindre {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ; et donne le succès, de grâce, à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} esclave aujourd’hui, et fais-lui trouver compassion devant cet homme. » Et moi, j’étais échanson du roi.
fr.B: De grâce, Seigneur, que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} oreille soit attentive à la prière de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur et à la prière de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs qui prennent plaisir à honorer {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom. Donne aujourd’hui le succès à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, et fais-lui trouver faveur auprès de cet homme. » J’étais alors échanson du roi.
fr.R: Seigneur, de grâce, écoute ma prière. Écoute les prières de tous {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs qui sont heureux de {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}honorer. Aide-moi aujourd’hui, et rends le roi bienveillant envers moi. » À cette époque, je servais le roi comme échanson.

sw.L: Nakusihi, Ee Bwana wangu, sikio {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} na liwe sikivu kwa sala ya mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na kwa sala ya watumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanaopendezwa kulicha jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; na umfanikishe, nakusihi, mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} leo, na umjalie kuhurumiwa mbele ya mtu huyu." Nami nilikuwa mnyweshaji wa mfalme.
sw.B: Ee Bwana, nakusihi, sikio {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} na lisikilize sala ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na sala ya watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanaofurahia kuliheshimu jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Umfanikishe mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} leo, umjalie rehema mbele ya mtu huyu." Wakati huo nilikuwa mnyweshaji wa mfalme.
sw.R: Ee Bwana, tafadhali sikiliza sala yangu. Sikiliza sala za watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wote wanaofurahi kukuheshimu. Unisaidie leo, umfanye mfalme anionee huruma." Wakati huo nilikuwa nikimtumikia mfalme kama mnyweshaji wake.

vi.L: Ôi, lạy Chúa của con, xin tai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chăm chú nghe lời cầu nguyện của nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và lời cầu nguyện của các nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là những người vui thích kính sợ danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và xin cho nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được thành công hôm nay, và cho người được thương xót trước mặt người này." Và tôi là quan dâng rượu của vua.
vi.B: Lạy Chúa, xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lắng tai nghe lời cầu nguyện của đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và của các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là những người vui lòng tôn kính danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Hôm nay xin cho đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được thành công và được thương xót trước mặt người này." Lúc ấy tôi làm quan dâng rượu cho vua.
vi.R: Lạy Chúa, xin lắng nghe lời cầu nguyện của con. Xin nghe lời cầu nguyện của tất cả các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là những người vui mừng tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Hôm nay xin giúp đỡ con, và xin khiến vua đối xử tử tế với con." Lúc ấy tôi phục vụ vua với chức quan dâng rượu.

ko.L: 아, 저의 주님, 부디 주님의 종의 기도와, 주님의 이름을 경외하기를 기뻐하는 주님의 종들의 기도에 주님의 귀를 기울여 주십시오. 그리고 부디 오늘 주님의 종이 형통하게 하시고, 이 사람 앞에서 그가 긍휼을 입게 해 주십시오." 그때 나는 왕의 술 맡은 관리였다.
ko.B: 주님, 주님의 종의 기도와 주님의 이름을 기쁘게 공경하는 주님의 종들의 기도에 귀를 기울여 주십시오. 오늘 주님의 종이 일을 이루게 하시고, 이 사람 앞에서 은혜를 입게 해 주십시오." 그때 나는 왕의 술 맡은 관리였다.
ko.R: 주님, 제 기도를 들어 주십시오. 기쁜 마음으로 주님을 공경하는 주님의 모든 종들의 기도를 들어 주십시오. 오늘 저를 도우셔서, 왕이 저에게 친절을 베풀게 해 주십시오." 그때 나는 왕의 술 맡은 관리로 왕을 섬기고 있었다.

pt.L: Por favor, meu Senhor, esteja, por favor, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ouvido atento à oração do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} escravo e à oração dos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} escravos que têm prazer em temer o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome; e dá êxito, por favor, ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} escravo hoje, e concede-lhe compaixão diante deste homem." E eu era copeiro do rei.
pt.B: Por favor, Senhor, que o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ouvido esteja atento à oração do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo e à oração dos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} servos que têm prazer em honrar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome. Dá êxito hoje ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo e concede-lhe misericórdia diante deste homem." Nessa época eu era o copeiro do rei.
pt.R: Por favor, Senhor, ouve a minha oração. Ouve as orações de todos os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} servos que têm alegria em {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} honrar. Ajuda-me hoje e faz com que o rei seja bondoso comigo." Naquela época eu servia o rei como seu copeiro.

decisions.choice: my Lord: Adonai, a title meaning master, used in address to God
decisions.reason: This is not the divine name of verse 5 but the title "Lord", in the form used only of God.

decisions.choice: delight to fear your name: gladly revere God
decisions.reason: To fear God's name is to hold him in awe and honor, which shows in obeying him (Deuteronomy 10:12; Psalm 86:11). God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known.

decisions.choice: compassion before this man: that the king will be kind and grant his request
decisions.reason: The word means mercy or kindness. "This man" is the king, as the sentence after it explains. Nehemiah is about to ask Artaxerxes a favor (2:1-8); before God the great king is only "this man".

decisions.choice: cupbearer: a trusted royal official who served the king's wine
decisions.reason: A cupbearer served the king his wine and guarded it from poison, so he had to be trusted and was often near the king (Genesis 40:1-13; 1 Kings 10:5). This gives Nehemiah the chance to speak to Artaxerxes (2:1).

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "honor" for "fear" here, since the word speaks of reverence, not terror. Literal keeps "fear".

decisions.choice: make the king kind to me
decisions.reason: Readable names "this man" as the king, as the next sentence does.

decisions.choice: "Señor" for Adonai, not in capitals; "copero" for the cupbearer
decisions.reason: Adonai is a title, not the divine name of verse 5, so it is written "Señor" with no setting. "Copero" as Genesis 40:1.

decisions.choice: "Seigneur" for Adonai, not in capitals; "échanson" for the cupbearer
decisions.reason: Adonai is a title, not the divine name of verse 5. "Échanson" as Genesis 40:1.

decisions.choice: "Bwana" for Adonai, not in capitals; "mnyweshaji" for the cupbearer
decisions.reason: Adonai is a title, not the divine name of verse 5. "Mnyweshaji" as Genesis 40:1.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for Adonai, not in capitals; "quan dâng rượu" for the cupbearer
decisions.reason: Adonai is a title, not the divine name of verse 5. "Quan dâng rượu" as Genesis 40:1.

decisions.choice: "주님" for Adonai; "술 맡은 관리" for the cupbearer
decisions.reason: Adonai is a title, not the divine name of verse 5, so it takes no span. "술 맡은 관리" as 1 Kings 10:5.

decisions.choice: o copeiro do rei
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "copeiro" is the word Genesis 40 and 1 Kings 10:5 use in Portuguese for the trusted official who served the king's wine (m4). Readable keeps it, since 2:1 shows what he did.

decisions.choice: meu Senhor (L); Senhor (B, R)
decisions.reason: Adonai, the title used of God (m1), is "Senhor" with only its first letter in capitals, as the Old Testament terms set it, so that it is not confused with the divine name in verse 5.
